1 خَرَتَ , (K,) aor.
خَرُتَ , inf. n. خَرْتٌ, (TK,) He perforated, bored, or pierced, (K,) the ear, (TK,) or a thing. (TA.) And خَرَتَ أَنْفَ الجَمَلِ [It perforated, or slit, (see the pass. part. n., below,) the nose of the camel]: said of the خِشَاش [or wooden thing that is inserted in the bone of the camel's nose]. (A.) ＝
-A2- خَرَتْنَا الأَرْضَ We knew the land and its roads. (Ks, S.) [Golius omits this; but mentions, as on the authority of Ibn-Maaroof, خَرِتَ, signifying He was skilful, or expert, in showing the way. What Ibn-Maaroof says, however, is that the inf. n. خَرَتٌ signifies the being acquainted with a road; and, with a place. See خِرِّيتُ.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
